content: Rilpivirine is associated with a known risk of prolonging the QTc interval, which can predispose patients to Torsades de Pointes, a potentially life-threatening arrhythmia. The following interactions and precautions should be considered when rilpivirine is co-administered with other drugs: 1. Itraconazole: Increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. No dose adjustment for rilpivirine is required. Monitor for breakthrough fungal infections when azole antifungals are co-administered. 2. Ketoconazole: Similar to itraconazole, it increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is necessary. 3. Lapatinib: Rilpivirine increases lapatinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 4. Levofloxacin: Rilpivirine increases levofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 5. Levoketoconazole: Increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. 6. Lithium: Both lithium and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 7. Lopinavir: Increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Rilpivirine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 8. Lumefantrine: Rilpivirine increases lumefantrine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 9. Magnesium salts (chloride, gluconate, oxide, sulfate): Decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces rilpivirine absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor therapy closely. 10. Methadone: Rilpivirine increases methadone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. No dose adjustments are required when initiating co-administration. Use with caution and monitor closely. 11. Mirtazapine: Both mirtazapine and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 12. Moxifloxacin: Rilpivirine increases moxifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 13. Nefazodone: Increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use with caution and monitor closely. 14. Nelfinavir: Increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use with caution and monitor closely. 15. Nilotinib: Rilpivirine increases nilotinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 16. Nizatidine: Decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, potentially leading to treatment failure or resistance. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor closely. 17. Nortriptyline: Rilpivirine increases nortriptyline toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 18. Octreotide: Rilpivirine increases octreotide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 19. Ofloxacin: Rilpivirine increases ofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 20. Olanzapine: Both olanzapine and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 21. Orlistat: Decreases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to virological failure. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 22. Osilodrostat: Both osilodrostat and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 23. Ozanimod: Both ozanimod and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients on QT-prolonging drugs with arrhythmogenic properties. Monitor closely. 24. Paliperidone: Rilpivirine increases paliperidone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 25. Pazopanib: Rilpivirine increases pazopanib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 26. Pentamidine: Rilpivirine increases pentamidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 27. Pimozide: Rilpivirine increases pimozide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 28. Posaconazole: Increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Rilpivirine increases posaconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. 29. Potassium chloride: Decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor closely. 30. Procainamide: Rilpivirine increases procainamide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 32. Propafenone: Rilpivirine increases propafenone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 33. Protriptyline: Rilpivirine increases protriptyline toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 34. Quetiapine: Rilpivirine increases quetiapine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 35. Quinidine: Rilpivirine increases quinidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 36. Quinine: Rilpivirine increases quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 37. Quizartinib: Both quizartinib and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered. 38. Ranolazine: Rilpivirine increases ranolazine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 39. Risperidone: Rilpivirine increases risperidone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 40. Ritonavir: Increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Rilpivirine increases ritonavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 41. Romidepsin: Rilpivirine increases romidepsin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 42. Selpercatinib: Increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 43. Sertraline: Both sertraline and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 44. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate: Decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Monitor closely. 45. Solifenacin: Both solifenacin and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 46. Sotalol: Rilpivirine increases sotalol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 47. Sunitinib: Rilpivirine increases sunitinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 48. Tacrolimus: Rilpivirine increases tacrolimus toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 49. Telavancin: Rilpivirine increases telavancin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 50. Thioridazine: Rilpivirine increases thioridazine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 51. Thiothixene: Rilpivirine increases thiothixene toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 52. Tipranavir: Increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect protease inhibitor plasma concentrations. Use with caution and monitor closely. 53. Toremifene: Rilpivirine increases toremifene toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 54. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous: Decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor closely. 55. Trimipramine: Rilpivirine increases trimipramine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 56. Ublituximab: Decreases rilpivirine effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Monitor closely. 57. Valbenazine: Both valbenazine and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 58. Vandetanib: Rilpivirine increases vandetanib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely.
